description:
## Signal

Rust's dead_code lint already proves there are no pub(crate)/pub(super)/private
functions kept alive only by tests: a non-test lib build has zero callers for such an
item and warns, and cargo build is clean under -D warnings.

The blind spot is fully-pub items, which the lint exempts as public API. Counting
consumers across src/ and tests/, 47 fully-pub functions have no non-test caller.

## Why this is not a mechanical delete

The 47 are not one population:

- Telemetry observation surfaces (events, events_named, count_by_kind, metadata_key)
  exist so tests can observe telemetry instead of asserting on internals. That is the
  intended direction, not debt.
- Fixture harness entry points (parse_fixture_metadata,
  fixture_matrix_paths_from_filename) are consumed by tests/fixture_matrix.rs, which
  IS the suite.
- Front doors (compile_root_jit) are public compiler API whose only current caller is
  a test.

Each class needs a different answer: keep, narrow visibility to pub(crate) so the lint
can see it, or delete with its test.

## Goal

Every fully-pub function either has a non-test consumer, or is narrowed so dead_code
governs it, or is deleted with the test that was its only reason to exist. After the
sweep the lint alone is a sufficient gate and this scan never needs repeating.

## Method

Reproduce the list with a consumer count over src/ + tests/ keyed on pub fn
definitions outside *_test.rs; classify each hit into the three buckets above before
touching anything.

## Origin

Found while merging main into fz-tfn/long-lived-recalculator (PR #118). The merge
applied the rule where it bore on a conflict: emitted_executables was deleted once
main removed its only consumer, and a test-only RootId import moved out of production
scope into the test module. The repo-wide sweep is separate work.
title: Sweep fully-pub functions whose only consumers are tests
